Анастасија Римљанка.“ — «Преп. муч.» is the `venerable-martyr` grade this corpus keeps in `types` and comes off, leaving the bare name with the by-name the heading prints. «Римљанка» is kept under section 6: it is a by-name and not a see — the woman of Rome, which is what the display name and the Russian form «Анастасия Римляныня» both say — and it is load-bearing, because the bare «Анастасија» is held by `anastasia-of-rome-15-april`, `anastasia-of-serbia` and `anastasia-the-patrician`, and one of those three is ALSO a woman of Rome. `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for the stored form and `sr-foldpred.mjs` predicts 0 other holders.

feast.note: Both of her life pages are headed «Дни памяти: 29 октября , 30 октября». The day page that lists her is the 29th; one row per church is the schema, so the 30th is recorded here and she does not render on it.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 29 октября ст. ст. — «Прмц. Анастасии Римляныни (ок. 249-259).»
source.note: The line is the first of the day and carries no typikon icon, so no rank is recorded. The name link titles her «Преподобномученица Анастасия Римляныня, Солунская» — of Thessalonica as well as of Rome — which no other page read for her repeats and which is not read into the folder.

attestations.note: The Russian agrees with the Romanian and Greek days this folder was written from and adds the governor's name, two hymns, and a second Russian day. **Its two lives of her differ from each other and from the Greek.** One has her orphaned at three and brought up in a monastery near Rome, twenty-one years old under Decius «(249-251 гг.)», her nails torn out, her hands and feet cut off, her teeth knocked out and her tongue cut, and beheaded; it also names a bystander, «некто Кирилл», who pitied her and gave her water and was killed for it as a secret Christian — the man this corpus holds as `cyril-martyr-29-october` off the Greek page for the same day. The other has the abbess Sophia bring her up, the governor Probus try flattery first, the tongue cut, the crowd's anger stop the torture, the beheading, the body thrown out to the beasts and Sophia find it and bury it. Both are kept in the life; nothing is chosen. The year is now the union of saint.gr's «περί το 256» and this line's «(ок. 249-259)».

source.text: doxologia.ro, 29 octombrie — «Sfânta Mare Muceniță Anastasia Romana»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 29ης Οκτωβρίου — «Αγία Αναστασία η Ρωμαία, η Οσιομάρτυς»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 29 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the woman is the folder's own: of Rome, rich parents, their fortune given to the poor, a monastery, and the governor Probus. The corpus's other Anastasias — of Rome with Basilissa on 15 April, the pupil of Chrysogonus, the Patrician — are none of them this one. A `dates` object is proposed from this page where the folder had none; the page's own reigns disagree with each other and the note on the interval says so. The proper apolytikion and the kontakion both name her and are taken; the Κάθισμα is neither a troparion nor a kontakion and is not drafted. No asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου».

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 11.11.2025 (29. октобар ст. ст.) — „Преп. муч. Анастасија Римљанка.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry and the longest on it, one person, quoted whole with the closing full stop the Prologue prints (BRIEF-SERBIAN section 4). `types` UNTOUCHED, AND THE RANK WORD IS WHY THAT NEEDS SAYING. The heading ranks her «Преп. муч.», which the brief’s table maps to `venerable-martyr` — a type this folder does NOT hold. It holds `great-martyr`, `virgin` and `monastic`, and those three together already carry everything «Преп. муч.» says: the martyrdom at a higher grade than the Prologue gives it, and the monastic life the «Преп.» stands for. Adding `venerable-martyr` beside `great-martyr` would make the folder claim two martyr grades for one woman on the word of the newer book, and a narrower rank word in a second book is no reason to re-rank a folder — the same reading made for `paraskeva-of-iconium` on the Julian 28 October. `dates` UNTOUCHED, AND THIS BOOK PUSHES AT THEM WITHOUT SETTLING ANYTHING. The folder holds `death` 249 to 259, «about 249 to 259», and its own note says the interval is two calendars and two readings with neither preferred: saint.gr has the governor Probus take her «περί το 256 μ.Χ.» and the Russian calendar prints «(ок. 249-259)». THIS ENTRY NAMES AN EMPEROR INSTEAD OF A YEAR: «Увенча се Анастасија венцем мученичким при цару Декију» — she was crowned with the martyr’s crown under the emperor Decius, whose reign this corpus elsewhere brackets 249 to 251. That agrees with the Russian floor and sits OUTSIDE the Greek year, so it is evidence for one of the two books the interval was built from — and narrowing on it would be preferring a calendar, which is not a reading of a page. Nothing moved; it is in the life and in the report. The entry also gives the governor’s name as Проб, which is saint.gr’s Πρόβος, and SEVENTEEN YEARS in the monastery before she became known, which is a span of her life and not a date. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS, AND IT IS MOSTLY HER OWN VOICE. She was ORPHANED AT THREE and taken into a women’s monastery near Rome whose abbess was SOPHIA, a nun at a high degree of perfection; AFTER SEVENTEEN YEARS she was spoken of all round about, among Christians as a great ascetic and AMONG THE HEATHEN AS A RARE BEAUTY, which is what brought the governor’s soldiers. THE ABBESS COUNSELLED HER FOR TWO HOURS on how to hold the faith, how to withstand flattering deceits and how to endure torture, and Anastasia answered „готово је срце моје за Христа страдати, готова је душа моја за сладчајшега Исуса умрети.“. Before the prince, turned first with promises and then with threats, she said „готова сам за Господа мога умрети не једанпут но – о кад би то могуће било – и сто пута!“. STRIPPED FOR MOCKERY SHE SHOUTED AT THE SERVANTS „бијте ме, и сеците, и трзајте, покрите ранама моје наго тело, и крвљу сакрите срам мој!“ — beat me, and cut, and tear, cover my naked body with wounds and hide my shame with blood. She thirsted twice and asked for water, and A CHRISTIAN NAMED CYRIL GAVE HER DRINK, FOR WHICH THE MARTYR BLESSED HIM AND THE HEATHEN BEHEADED HIM. HER BREASTS AND HER TONGUE WERE CUT OFF. AN ANGEL OF GOD KEPT APPEARING AND HOLDING HER UP. And AT THE LAST THE BLESSED SOPHIA FOUND HER BODY AND BURIED IT HONOURABLY. NO NEW `related`. `cyril-martyr-29-october` is already related both ways and is linked in the new paragraph — this book is the first of the four to say what he did and what it cost him. SOPHIA THE ABBESS GETS NOTHING: she is narrated and in no heading, which is Ruling 3 and section 5, and no folder in this corpus is her — the five Sophias it keeps are of Aenus, of Kleisoura, the mother of Faith, Hope and Love, and the martyrs of 18 September and 18 December. The governor Probus and the emperor Decius are narrated and in no heading either. No `locations`: Rome and a monastery near it are named and neither is proposed as a coordinate on this folder. THE FORM IS FREE BECAUSE IT KEEPS THE BY-NAME: `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Анастасија Римљанка», and names three folders for the bare «Анастасија». The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day’s verse is Bishop Nikolai’s own and is about Abraham.

hymns.text: Mielușeaua Ta, Iisuse, Anastasia, strigă cu glas mare: pe Tine, Mirele meu, Te iubesc și pe Tine căutându-Te mă chinuiesc și împreună mă răstignesc și împreună mă îngrop cu Botezul Tău; și pătimesc pentru Tine, ca să împărățesc întru Tine; și mor pentru Tine, ca să viez pentru Tine; ci, ca o jertfă fără de prihană, primește-mă pe mine ceea ce cu dragoste mă jertfesc Ție. Pentru rugăciunile ei, ca un Milostiv, mântuiește sufletele noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, Troparul Sfintei Cuvioase Mucenițe Anastasia Romana, Glasul 4

english.text: Thy lamb Anastasia, O Jesus, cries out with a loud voice: Thee, my Bridegroom, I love; and seeking Thee I am in torment; with Thee I am crucified and with Thee buried in Thy baptism; I suffer for Thee that I may reign in Thee, and I die for Thee that I may live for Thee. Receive me, then, as a spotless sacrifice, who offer myself to Thee in love. By her prayers, as the Merciful One, save our souls.

hymns.text: Ἀσκήσει ἐκλάμψασα ὥσπερ παρθένος σεμνή ἀθλήσεως αἵμασι τὴν τῆς ἁγνείας στολὴν ἐνθέως ἐφοίνιξας· ὅθεν, Ἀναστασία, ὡς ὁσία καὶ μάρτυς, χάριτας ἰαμάτων ἀποστράπτεις ἐν κόσμῳ πρεσβεύουσα τῷ Σωτῆρι ὑπὲρ τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος δ’, Ταχύ προκατάλαβε — the first hymn on the page of «Αγία Αναστασία η Ρωμαία, η Οσιομάρτυς». It names her and no other saint.

english.text: Shining out in asceticism as a modest virgin, with the blood of your contest you dyed the robe of your purity in a godly way; and so, Anastasia, as both nun and martyr, you flash out graces of healing in the world, interceding with the Saviour for our souls.

hymns.text: Παρθενίας vάμασι, καθηγvισμέvη ὁσία, μαρτυρίου αἵμασιν, Ἀvαστασία πλυθεῖσα, παρέχεις τοῖς ἐν ἀνάγκαις τῶν νοσημάτων, ἴασιν καὶ σωτηρίαν τοῖς προσιοῦσιν, ἐκ καρδίας, ἰσχὺν γᾶρ νέμει, Χριστὸς ὁ βρύωv, χάριν ἀέναον.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον — on the page of «Αγία Αναστασία η Ρωμαία, η Οσιομάρτυς». It names her and no other saint. The readings «vάμασι», «Ἀvαστασία», «βρύωv» and «γᾶρ» are the page's own and are copied as they stand.

english.text: Hallowed in the streams of virginity, holy one, and washed in the blood of martyrdom, Anastasia, you grant healing and salvation to those in the straits of sickness who come to you from the heart; for Christ, who wells up unfailing grace, gives you the strength.

hymns.text: Агница Твоя, Иисусе, Анастасия/ зовет велиим гласом:/ Тебе, Женише мой, люблю,/ и, Тебе ищущи, страдальчествую,/ и сраспинаюся, и спогребаюся Крещению Твоему,/ и стражду Тебе ради,/ яко да царствую в Тебе,/ и умираю за Тя, да и живу с Тобою,/ но, яко жертву непорочную, приими мя,/ с любовию пожершуюся Тебе.// Тоя молитвами яко Милостив спаси души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 29 октября ст. ст. — «Тропарь преподобномученицы Анастасии Римляныни»
source.note: The common of a woman martyr, with her name set into it, printed under her own heading, which makes it hers (BRIEF.md §4).

english.text: Your lamb, Jesus, Anastasia, cries out with a great voice: you, my Bridegroom, I love; and seeking you I contend, and am crucified and buried with you in your baptism; and I suffer for your sake, that I may reign in you, and I die for you that I may also live with you. Receive me as an unblemished sacrifice, offered to you in love. By her prayers, as you are merciful, save our souls.

hymns.text: Девства водами очищенна, преподобная,/ мученичества кровьми, Анастасие, венчавшися,/ подаеши сущим в нуждах недугов исцеление и спасение,/ приступающим от сердца,/ крепость бо тебе подает Христос,// источая благодать приснотекущую.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 29 октября ст. ст. — «Кондак преподобномученицы Анастасии Римляныни»

english.text: Cleansed by the waters of virginity, venerable one, and crowned with the blood of martyrdom, Anastasia, you give healing of sicknesses and salvation to those in need who come to you from the heart; for Christ grants you strength, pouring out grace that never fails.

death.note: Two calendars and two readings, and neither is preferred. saint.gr: «Όταν τη συνέλαβε ο ηγεμόνας Πρόβος (περί το 256 μ.Χ.)». days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 29 октября ст. ст. prints «(ок. 249-259)», and both of its lives set the persecution under «императоре Декии (249-251 гг.)», whose reign the Greek year falls outside. The interval is the union of the two, which is the Russian line's own span.
